title:
Space engineering
Communications guidelines
organisation: ECSS Secretariat, ESA-ESTEC Requirements & Standards Division (prepared by the ECSS-E-HB-50 Working Group)
status_notes: First issue, dated 15 November 2008 (change log, p. 3). The handbook is informative and not binding, and the ECSS standards prevail in any conflict (scope, p. 17). It describes the 2008 generation of ECSS-E-ST-50-0x standards, which were later superseded by the ECSS-E-AS-50-2x adoption notices (see ecss-e-st-50c-rev-1-1march2021, p. 20). The 2021 ECSS-E-ST-50C Rev.1 still cites ECSS-E-HB-50 in its bibliography and in requirement 5.4.9a.
summary:
The informative **ECSS communications handbook**, the companion to ECSS-E-ST-50 and its Level-3 data-link, coding, RF and on-board bus standards. It explains how the ECSS E-50 standards and the related CCSDS Recommended Standards fit together into a coherent protocol stack, evaluates issues that the standards cannot discuss, and gives guidance on option selection.

Section 3 is a primer on CCSDS document colours (Blue, Green, Magenta, Orange, Yellow, Silver), the withdrawal of ESA PSS standards, and ECSS's then-policy of re-publishing modified CCSDS books, which was being replaced by adoption notices. Tables 3-1 and 3-2 list each covered standard with its 2008 issue and date, and an OSI-layer map shows where each one sits.

Section 4 has one chapter per standard, each giving purpose, description, *differences from CCSDS*, options and recommended practice. It covers ECSS-E-ST-50, ranging/Doppler, RF and modulation (including the 'transponder dual lock' issue), TM coding, the TM transfer frame, the TC protocols (14 documented differences from CCSDS 231/232, e.g. the Packet Assembly Controller and one frame per CLTU), AOS, Proximity-1, Space Packet and Encapsulation, IPv4/IPv6, PUS (field usage and reserved APIDs 0 and 2047), CFDP, SCIDs, compression, time codes, SpaceWire, MIL-1553 and discrete interfaces.

Section 5 covers cross-cutting topics such as channel coding options, playback of recorded frames, idle data, security, interoperability and PICS. Section 6 recounts the history of CCSDS (TC/TM, AOS, Proximity-1, CFDP, DTN, SOIS) and gives applicability tables. Annexes A-F are draft **PICS proformas** for the sending and receiving ends of ECSS-E-ST-50-01, -03 and -04, and Annex G gives false-decoding probabilities for RS E=8 with 4D-8PSK-TCM. This is a good map of the European space-link protocol landscape around 2008.

key_points.text: The handbook is informative best practice and is not binding; in case of conflict the ECSS standards prevail.
The E-50 series covers the space link and space network in detail and the ground network only as needed for end-to-end services; other ground aspects belong to the ECSS E-70 series.

CCSDS publication categories: Blue Books (Recommended Standards), Green (Informational Reports), Magenta (Recommended Practices), Orange (Experimental), Yellow (Record) and Silver (Historical, with '-S' appended to the number).
ESA PSS communication standards were modified versions of CCSDS recommendations; all PSS documents have been withdrawn in favour of ECSS or CCSDS standards.

ECSS differs from CCSDS in having the ESA-developed PUS (ECSS-E-ST-70-41) as an application layer and in combining the TC protocols into the single ECSS-E-ST-50-04. Modifying CCSDS books was being phased out in favour of adoption notices.

In 2008 the covered issues were the 'C' editions of 31 July 2008 for E-ST-50, -01, -02, -03, -04, -05, -12 and -14 and 15 Nov 2008 for -13, with -11 (SpaceWire protocols) to be published; ECSS-E-ST-70-41 was issue A of 30 Jan 2003.

Other covered standards and issues: CCSDS 133.0-B-1 (Sep 2003), 133.1-B-1 (Jun 2006), 135.0-B-3 (Oct 2006), 301.0-B-3 (Jan 2002), 320.0-B-5 (Sep 2007), 727.0-B-4 (Jan 2007) and 732.0-B-2 (Jul 2006); for AOS there was no ECSS standard, only CCSDS 732.0-B.
The space link protocols are mapped onto five OSI layers (physical, data link, network, transport, application); CFDP spans transport and application, and Proximity-1 spans data link and physical.

'Transponder dual lock': when both receivers lock, one near its threshold (about -122 dBm), telecommands can be rejected; Cryosat-2 combines both LGA signals with a 3 dB hybrid; see report TEC-ETC/2008.66/PMcM.

ECSS-E-ST-50-04 includes the optional Packet Assembly Controller, inherited from PSS, so its minimum TC segment is one octet (CCSDS: two). European hardware uses the PAC, but European missions generally do not use segmentation.
In CCSDS several TC frames may share one CLTU; in ECSS-E-ST-50-04 a CLTU contains exactly one frame, for reliability and compatibility with European hardware.

ECSS-E-ST-70-41 (2003) still calls the packets 'telemetry source packet' and 'telecommand packet' and the secondary header the 'Data Field Header'; it reserves APID 2047 (idle) and APID 0 (time), while CCSDS 135.0-B also reserves 2045-2046 and 2040-2044.
PUS makes the 16-bit Packet Error Control field mandatory on TC packets and optional (fixed per APID) on TM; it was not yet in CCSDS 133.0-B-1.

Playback of recorded TM frames by asynchronous insertion uses a dedicated VC; in forward mode recorded ASMs must use the alternative pattern 0x352EF853, and recorded CLCWs must not be processed by the real-time TC system.
Applicability guidance: ECSS-E-ST-50-05 and CCSDS 301.0-B for all missions; AOS for very large return data volumes; Proximity-1 for inter-spacecraft links; ECSS-E-ST-70-41 for all ESA missions.
For ground components the handbook points to the EGOS portal (SCOS-2000, SIMSAT, ground station systems, ESA SLE Gateway).
Annexes A-F are draft PICS proformas for the sending and receiving ends of ECSS-E-ST-50-01, ECSS-E-ST-50-03 and ECSS-E-ST-50-04.
For the R-S E=8 code (interleaving I=8) concatenated with 4D-8PSK-TCM, the false decoding probability stays below 1e-19 when the mean BER is below 1e-9 or the FER below 5e-7, which is negligible.

notes: Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers, and PDF page 262 is blank (the registry gives 261 pages). The text extraction uses Unicode non-breaking hyphens (U+2010/U+2011) in identifiers such as 'ECSS‐E‐HB‐50A', so plain-hyphen searches can miss them. The reference list (pp. 259-261) is headed 'References' and, by its stated convention, mostly omits issue numbers. Its explanation of specific-issue references gives 'ECSS-E-ST-50-01' as an example without any issue letter (p. 259). Table 3-1 lists ECSS-E-ST-50-11 as 'SpaceWire protocols, To be published' (p. 27), while the reference list calls it 'SpaceWire RMAP protocol' (p. 260). The handbook describes PUS issue A (2003), and ECSS-E-ST-70-41C (2016) post-dates it. Annex G curves and many figures are images or scrambled text. Some false-decoding curve captions say RS(255,239) while the table titles say RS(254,238) (pp. 256-258).
